2026-08-26.headline: Light day: Edge gets process isolation toggles, Defender renames a preview setting, and Linux renames a category to keep us on our toes.
highlights: Windows: Microsoft Edge adds 6 new settings including 'Enable Process Isolation' with device and user variants, plus clipboard suggestions for the address bar; the isolation toggle looks like a smart security hardening option
Windows: Microsoft Edge default settings also pick up the clipboard suggestion toggle, so you can set a baseline users can override
Windows: Defender's 'Controlled Configuration' is now 'Configuration Protection (Preview)', a pure rename, no functional change expected
Linux: The 'Advanced Protection' category got renamed to 'Advanced Settings', pure picker reorganization with no impact on existing profiles
2026-08-26.watchOut: Defender's Configuration Protection had its option list touched (still 3 options), so if you rely on it, double-check the available values didn't shift. Otherwise, no removals or breaking changes.

2026-08-18.headline: Apple finally gets the web-filtering memo: new Web Content Filter and DNS Proxy settings for iOS/macOS, while Windows Update for Business discovers the concept of a calendar.
highlights: iOS and macOS: Web Content Filter and DNS Proxy bring per-app and per-domain blocking, plugin-based filtering, and a 'Browsers' toggle on iOS. Say goodbye or hello to productivity, depending on how you configure.
macOS: 38 Content Cache settings let you control peer caching, cache limits, and even keep the Mac awake for sharing. Because your network's bandwidth is apparently a team sport.

Windows: Maintenance Windows for Windows Update for Business let you set schedule types (weekly, monthly), start times, and actions. Finally, a way to keep updates from hitting at 9 AM during your stand-up.
2026-08-18.watchOut: No settings were removed, but 271 categories vanished from the picker. That's reorganization, not an apocalypse; existing policies are fine. The two 'changed' categories are likely metadata nits, so don't lose sleep.

2026-08-06.headline: A sleepy Summer day in the Settings Catalog: just one Linux setting got its internal ID swapped, nothing to see here.
highlights: Linux: 'Platform Update Fixed Version' changed its internal identifier from 'version' to 'fixedVersion'. Everything else stays the same for now.
2026-08-06.watchOut: No operational impact expected, but if you've hard-coded the old offsetUri in any automation, update those references before Microsoft sweeps the old one away.

2026-08-02.headline: Android Enterprise lost a few toys today: eSIM wipe controls, work profile lock requirements, and screen timeout settings all got the boot. Time to check your existing policies before something quietly stops applying.
highlights: Android: 2 settings removed from General, including 'Remove all eSIMs during a device wipe' and 'Maximum days to turn off work profile' - if you relied on those, you'll need a new way to enforce eSIM cleanup or lockout limits.
Android: 2 more settings pulled from an unknown category (screen on while plugged in, screen timeout), so kiosk and dedicated device configurations lose some display control.
Android: 'Require separate work lock' removed from Work profile password settings - previously enforced a distinct lock for work apps, now gone.
2026-08-02.watchOut: No changed fields, but these removals could break existing profiles that referenced these settings. Verify your Android Enterprise configurations still do what you expect, especially for device wipe and lock screen policies.

2026-08-01.headline: Quiet day: one new Windows security setting to enforce Entra ID auth, a tweak to transport options, and a category shuffle.
highlights: Windows: New 'Enable Microsoft Entra ID Authentication Enforcement' under Security; worth a look if you want to force Entra ID sign-in.
Windows: 'Select Transport Type' under Connections had its option list modified, still 3 options, so check your current policy if you use it.
The 'Power' category was removed from the catalog; if you had policies there, verify they're still around or if they moved.
2026-08-01.watchOut: The Power category removal could leave existing policies without a home, and the transport option changes might alter behavior; worth a quick audit.

2026-07-30.headline: Defender gains AI Agent protection, iOS/macOS get fine-grained app permission controls, and Microsoft shuffled thousands of settings into new categories.
highlights: Windows: Defender now offers AI Agent Protection and AI Agent Network Inspection, worth configuring before agents start wandering your network.

iOS/macOS: A wave of new App Settings lets you police per-app permissions (camera, mic, location) with signing ID and path prefix rules, so you can finally say no to that flashlight app that wants your location.
Linux: Platform Update scheduling arrives, letting you pin a fixed version and set update windows; no more surprise midnight kernel swaps.
Windows: Microsoft Edge picks up a few security hardening settings (strict MIME for workers, socket pool randomization) for the edge-curious.
2026-07-30.watchOut: Two UAC settings now require a newer minimum Windows build (26100.7019); check your eligible devices before they go silent. Also, 3,903 settings were moved to new categories, so expect some heads-down re-browsing.

2026-07-22.headline: Windows App gets a policy home with update rings and idle logoff; OneDrive adds OIDC for on-prem SharePoint sync and lets you mandate the sync folder name.
highlights: Windows: New Windows App category, 8 settings to control automatic updates, admin release ring, inactivity timeout with logoff, and skip first-run experience.
Windows: OneDrive grows 12 settings, including OIDC auth for on-prem SharePoint sync, custom folder naming, web offline mode blocking, and hard-delete on unmount (use with care).
Windows: Win RE (Recovery Environment) gets enable/remediate toggles; worth a look if you rely on BitLocker recovery.
Windows: Edge adds Copilot address bar suggestion controls (user and machine), plus some Web Worker data URL tweaks.

2026-07-17.headline: Windows debloat is here: remove unwanted Store apps one by one, or hand over a list; plus WSL registry allowlist and Linux AV 'Audit' mode.
highlights: Windows: 27 new App Package Deployment settings let you remove specific built-in Store apps (Teams, Photos, Copilot, Xbox clutter) or use a dynamic list for a rolling purge. Your debloat dreams, management-approved.
Windows: WSL container settings add a registry allowlist; worth enforcing before someone pulls a questionable image.
Linux: Antivirus engine 'Enforcement Level' gains a 4th option: Audit, which logs detections without blocking. Great for testing without disruption.
2026-07-17.watchOut: No removals or breaking changes; the 26 applicability updates simply extend support to Windows build 26200, so existing policies now cover the latest release.

2026-07-10.headline: Intune adds 8 new Privilege Management settings to define elevation rules; now you can decide exactly who gets the 'admin for a day' pass, down to the individual user.
highlights: Windows: 8 new Endpoint Privilege Management settings for elevation action, validation, and user applicability lists, so you can grant specific apps to specific people without carpet-bombing admin rights.
Also new: rule name and setting type fields, making it easier to organize and audit your elevation policies.
Connectivity's 'Disable Cross Device Resume (User)' had its 2 options reshuffled; same count, likely just a label change, but give it a glance if you rely on it.
2026-07-10.watchOut: No removals and no functional breakage; the only change is a cosmetic option reordering in that one Connectivity setting, so you're safe to roll out without panic.

2026-07-01.headline: Slow day in the Settings Catalog: Windows picks up a single new setting, 'Configure Camera Options', and that is all. No removals, no fire drills.
highlights: Windows: One new setting in the Camera category, 'Configure Camera Options'; the name suggests some control over camera behavior, but the catalog isn't saying more.

2026-07.headline: Windows takes center stage with per-app removal toggles for in-box Store apps and a WSL registry allowlist to keep containers from pulling surprises.
2026-07.overview: July came with five update days, and Windows soaked up most of the attention, finally offering admins the debloat controls they've been nagging about for years. Apple also got a privacy-permission boost in App Settings, while Linux picked up update scheduling and a memory scan preview. The rest was mostly picker gardening: nearly four thousand category renames, description reformatting, and a few applicability bumps that are worth a second glance if you've got assignments pinned to old OS versions.

sections.body: The headline act is 27 App Package Deployment settings that let you remove specific in-box Store apps (Teams, Photos, Xbox stuff, Office leftovers) plus a dynamic list for rolling debloat. WSL containers also got an allowlist for allowed registries, which is a smart security control if you don't want someone pulling an image from somewhere imaginative. OneDrive gained OIDC authentication against on-prem SharePoint and offline mode restrictions, Edge picked up CPU tier overrides and stricter MIME checks, and Defender added AI agent protection and network inspection. Don't overlook the new Writing Assistance blocklists or the Privilege Management elevation rules. The applicability for those Store app settings was bumped to support the 26200 build, so they'll behave on newer Windows insiders.

Apple scored a chunk of new App Settings covering privacy permissions (Location, Microphone, Camera, etc.) on both iOS and macOS, with analogous Safari Browser defaults for sites. macOS got a few Restrictions to force Wi-Fi and captive portal connections from the lock screen, and iOS/macOS picked up Siri and Intelligence toggles (like Force Reduce Sensitive Content and Allow Natural Language Editing). A few Privacy Preferences Policy Control entries got marked as deprecated, so clean up any profiles still referencing them.

Android was quiet but practical: you can now remove all eSIMs during a device wipe, set a maximum number of days before the work profile turns off, and enforce a separate work lock. A couple of power settings (screen timeout, stay awake while plugged in) round out the month.

Linux got update scheduling via Platform Update settings, letting you define windows and fixed versions, which is a welcome relief for admins who like predictability. Defender also added a memory scan (preview) and gained an extra enforcement level to make that scan useful.

2026-07.watchOut: The applicability changes for the Store app removal settings now target 26200 as a max, but two UAC settings (Admin Approval Mode and elevation prompt) got their minimum bumped to 10.0.26100.7019; if you're on an older build they'll silently no-apply. Also, the Smart Card Removal Behavior picked up a new option, so verify your configured value didn't shift, and if you script against category IDs, the huge reorg this month will break those scripts.

2026-06-25.headline: Edge picks up a few new Copilot dials (CPU tier, address bar suggestions) and you get Local Fonts controls; meanwhile, two Wallet features get the official 'Deprecated' tattoo.
highlights: macOS, Windows: 4 new Copilot-related settings, including 'Override for the CPU performance tier' and 'Enable Copilot address bar suggestions', let you tune how aggressively Copilot muscles into the browser
macOS, Windows: Local Fonts permission now has a default plus per-site allow/block lists, so you can keep sites from fingerprinting via installed fonts
macOS, Windows: 'Wallet Donation Enabled' and 'Edge Wallet E-Tree Enabled' are renamed with '(Deprecated)', likely heading for the chopping block

macOS: One setting lost its macOS applicability, 'Allows web pages to use identifiers for the purpose of protected content playback' is now Windows-only; if you had that on Macs, it's no longer effective
2026-06-25.watchOut: The protected content playback setting dropped macOS support, so any policy relying on it for Macs will silently stop applying; also, 63 description rewrites are just textual cleanup, no behavior change, but the deprecated Wallet flags suggest cleanup is coming.

2026-06-24.headline: Android Enterprise just got a whole new 'Connectivity' lockdown cabinet: block calls, SMS, 2G, airplane mode, and more; meanwhile Windows Autopilot apps allowed jumped from 10 to 25, so you can finally deploy more than a handful.
highlights: Android Enterprise: new 'Connectivity' category with 11 settings to block outgoing calls, SMS, 2G, airplane mode, network resets, and even configuring VPN or cell broadcasts. Kiosk and 'please don't embarrass me' devices just got a big security upgrade.

Windows Autopilot device prep: 'Allowed applications' limit raised from 10 to 25 (via description change), so you can pack more apps into that deployment without juggling. Scripts stay at 10, but now explicitly say 'Windows PowerShell' and point to the new report.
Windows: new User Rights setting 'Adjust Memory Quotas For Process' shows up; handy for power users or your friendly neighborhood memory-hogging app.

tvOS and visionOS Setup Assistant additions: new toggles for Screen Saver, TV Provider Sign In, TV Room, TV Home Screen Sync, Tips, and Tap to Setup. Apple TV and Vision Pro admins, you have something to do now
2026-06-24.watchOut: 39 Windows App Package Deployment settings (Remove Default Store packages, Feedback Hub, Outlook, etc.) got a maximum supported version of 10.0.26100.8116. If you're on a newer build, these may stop applying, so check your device builds before you redeploy. Also, 3 OOBE 'Hide' settings had their option lists tweaked (count unchanged), worth a peek if you use them.

2026-06-10.headline: Edge Copilot gets the chokehold: new URL allow/block lists, new tab page control, and developer tools lockdown land for Windows and macOS.
highlights: Windows and macOS: New 'Browsing with Copilot Allowed/Blocked URLs' policies let you decide exactly where Copilot can browse, plus a setting to auto-open the side pane with contextual insights from Outlook links. The debloat of Copilot begins now.
Windows and macOS: Developer tools get URL pattern allow/block lists, so you can keep the F12 crowd from their favorite pastime on specific sites.
Windows and macOS: New Tab Page now lets you set the default feed tab to Work or Discover and choose which tabs appear. Because nothing says productivity like a curated new tab page.
Windows and macOS: 'Allow M365 authentication popups in work profiles' finally lets your users authenticate without the popup blocker throwing a hissy fit.
2026-06-10.watchOut: 111 Edge policy descriptions got rewritten; mostly grammar and clarity, but if you have those policies, give them a quick glance to ensure the intended behavior matches the new wording. No functional removals or deprecations today, so you're safe.

2026-06.headline: June gave Android Enterprise a connectivity lockdown kit and Edge a pile of Copilot and dev-tools controls.
2026-06.overview: Three update days, and the highlights are Android security toggles and Edge AI governance. Android got blocks for 2G, SMS, and eSIM; Edge gained a dozen Copilot controls plus dev-tools URL allow/deny. The rest was housekeeping: 176 Edge descriptions rewritten for clarity, 41 Windows app removal settings bumped to a specific build, and a few Setup Assistant additions for Apple TV and Vision Pro.

sections.body: Windows got one new User Right (Adjust Memory Quotas) and a lot of Edge settings alongside macOS: Copilot side pane automation, developer tools URL block/allow lists, local fonts permission controls, and a new tab page feed toggle. The 41 App Package Deployment settings (removal toggles for in-box apps) now carry a maximum supported OS version of 26100.8116, which is technically new information but probably means they still work exactly as before. No breaking changes here, just fresh levers to pull.

macOS shares the Edge expansion with Windows, so you get the Copilot and dev-tools controls on Macs too, plus a couple of local font permission settings. Over on Apple TV, Setup Assistant gained Screen Saver, TV Provider Sign In, TV Room, and Home Screen Sync toggles; visionOS picked up a Tips toggle; and iOS/tvOS both got Tap to Setup. Useful for zero-touch deployment flows, nothing that'll rock your world.

Android Enterprise is where the action is: 11 new Connectivity settings let you block outgoing calls, SMS, 2G, airplane mode, network resets, VPN configuration, ultra wideband, and more. General adds eSIM, wallpaper, user icon, and printing blocks. Applications adds widget blocking and blocking apps from exposing functions. If you've got fully managed devices, this is the lockdown you've been waiting for. Just don't forget to actually enable them before someone finds the 2G fallback.

2026-06.watchOut: The Windows App Package Deployment settings now have a maximum supported OS version (10.0.26100.8116). If you assigned them without a version filter, devices on a later build won't get them, so recheck your assignments. Also, a few Edge wallet settings were renamed with '(Deprecated)' in the display name; update any automation or documentation that references them by name.

2026-05-27.headline: Edge gets a Copilot control room (28 new settings) and macOS finally gets local account automation, so you can stop babysitting device setup.
highlights: Windows: 28 new Edge settings to govern Copilot: enable the new tab page, allow/block browsing with Copilot URL lists, and constrain devtools to specific URL patterns. Perfect for when the AI starts browsing where it shouldn't.

macOS: New Account settings category with 10 settings for local primary/admin account creation, admin password rotation periods, prefill info, and hiding accounts. Pair with Setup Assistant to automate enrollment without a human holding hands.

iOS/macOS: Setup Assistant picks up toggles for App Store, OS showcase, FileVault, Auto unlock with Apple Watch, and more; iOS adds Safety and handling, Web Content Filtering, Multitasking, and Camera button. Tinker away.
Windows: Security Settings adds 4 old-school DCOM/OLE blocks (insecure protocols, OLE Graph, OrgChart, FPRPC fallback) - lock those down before someone exploits a legacy component.
2026-05-27.watchOut: 31 settings got renamed, mostly with '(Deprecated)' tacked on Apple restrictions like Genmoji, Image Playground, Dictation, and Visual Intelligence. They're on the way out, so if you use them, find replacements before the rug gets pulled. Also, Agent Governance 'Agent user account' gained an option (1 to 2), so double-check your existing config.

2026-05-21.headline: New Agent Governance settings on Windows give you a leash for agents: control their user, access level, and what they can touch on disk and network.
highlights: Windows: Agent Governance category arrives with 9 settings; set an agent user, access level, allowed filesystem directories, and network access. Time to decide if Copilot gets VIP or a bathroom break pass.
Windows: One App Package Deployment setting (specify additional package family names) retired, probably absorbed elsewhere.

2026-05.headline: Windows gains Agent Governance and a flood of Edge Copilot settings, while macOS adds local account creation and Apple deprecates a stack of Intelligence restrictions.
2026-05.overview: Two update days in May, and the month belongs to Windows: a brand new Agent Governance category for controlling AI agents, plus a wave of Edge settings around Copilot and New Tab Page feeds. Apple added macOS local account creation and Setup Assistant toggles, while marking a heap of Apple Intelligence restrictions as deprecated. Android got one Bluetooth sharing toggle and nothing else.

sections.body: Windows gets a new Agent Governance category to control AI agent behavior: filesystem access rules, network access, execution toggles, and an agent user account option that gained a second choice. Edge picked up 28 settings for Copilot URL allowlists/blocklists, developer tools restrictions, and WebSocket connection limits, plus 12 New Tab Page settings to force the Work or Discover feed. A few user-level security settings (Block Insecure Protocols, OLE Graph, etc.) also landed, plus a new MAM enrollment toggle when Purview DLP is configured. But note that App Package Deployment lost its 'Specify additional package family names to remove' setting.

macOS gained Account settings for creating local admin and primary accounts during setup, with password rotation and user affinity options, plus Setup Assistant toggles for FileVault, Apple Watch unlock, and iCloud Storage. iOS picked up Setup Assistant toggles for Web Content Filtering and the Camera button. Both platforms saw a wave of Apple Intelligence restrictions marked '(Deprecated)', including Assistant, Dictation, Image Playground, and others, so those are on the way out. Also new is an SSO setting to enable first user creation during setup.
Android Enterprise got exactly one setting: Block Bluetooth sharing. That's it, nothing else to see here.

2026-05.watchOut: Rework any profiles using 'Specify additional package family names to remove' from App Package Deployment, as that setting is gone. The Apple Intelligence restrictions now labeled '(Deprecated)' are likely to be removed in a future release, so start planning replacements.

2026-04-30.headline: Edge gets a dump truck of new macOS and Windows policies, macOS especially with 67 new settings including scareware blocker, local network request controls, and TLS 1.3 Early Data toggles; Linux Defender also picks up scheduled scans and offline definition updates.
highlights: macOS Edge: 67 new policies, including blocking sites from hitting the local network, scareware protection, and IPv6 reachability checks. Because your browser should not have the keys to the LAN.
Windows Edge: InPrivate URL allow/block lists, guest mode enforcement, and foreground tab priority. Now you can decide which URLs survive the 'Clearing Browsing Data' button.
Linux Defender: New Schedule Scan and Antivirus engine settings (10 + 6) for offline definitions and low-CPU scans. Finally, you can schedule a hunt for malware without waking the whole fleet.
Edge 'Enhance the security state' policies are now marked obsolete. Time to migrate to the security baseline, folks.
2026-04-30.watchOut: Cross Device Resume now requires Windows 10 build 26100.7705 or later, so existing policies will quietly stop applying to outdated devices; also, several Edge policies were renamed or marked obsolete, so check your configurations against the new names.

2026-04.headline: April was the month of the browser: Edge got a truckload of new toggles (including Scareware blocker and local network access control) while Linux Defender remembered scheduling exists.
2026-04.overview: One update day, but it was busy if you live in Edge. Over 80 new Edge settings across Windows and macOS, plus the long-awaited Linux scan scheduling and some Windows device lock and OOBE controls. Rest was housekeeping: 162 description rewrites and a handful of renames.

sections.body: Windows got a few real nuggets: Device Lock now offers the classic password age/complexity/history quartet, useful if you still enforce passwords. OOBE got 'hide change account options' and an update install toggle for the first-run experience. App Package Deployment gained a device-wide 'additional package family names to remove' option, giving debloaters another arrow. Edge on Windows picked up 14 new settings: InPrivate URL allow/block lists, guest mode enforcement, XSLT kill switch, and more. Also, Disable Cross Device Resume now requires build 26100.7705 or later, so check your ring if you have that policy.

macOS is where Edge exploded: 67 new settings, covering everything from TLS 1.3 Early Data control to a GenAI local model setting and a Scareware blocker that can share URLs with Defender SmartScreen. iOS got one Extensible SSO addition: Enable Registration During Setup, nice for zero-touch. Plenty of description rewrites in Edge, but nothing that changes behavior.

One rename and one new option: the location toggle went from 'Block location' to 'Location' and grew from 2 to 3 options. Probably adding 'ask' or similar, but you'll have to look. Existing 'block' policies should still work, but recheck if you were relying on the old two-state.

Defender for Linux finally got scheduling: weekly or daily scans with 'run when idle' and 'randomize start time', plus offline definition update fallback to cloud and an update interval setting. If you've been pushing scans via cron, you can now do it through the catalog.

2026-04.watchOut: The Disable Cross Device Resume applicability bump to minimum 10.0.26100.7705 will silently stop applying on older builds, so bump your update rings if you still rely on that policy. Also, the Android location setting changed shape, so verify any existing policy didn't assume two options.

2026-03-26.headline: New Windows network protections, Apple Intelligence controls, and Mac recovery lock management land in the Settings Catalog, while a batch of Edge policies gets deprecation tags.
highlights: Windows: 22 new network settings to block or allow sites from reaching local network endpoints or the local device, a solid defense against browser-based local network snooping; plus 8 cryptography compliance policies to enforce TLS cipher and key exchange preferences.

iOS and macOS: A new Intelligence Settings category gives admins granular control over Apple Intelligence features like Smart Replies, Image Playground, Writing Tools, and Genmoji, with additional Siri and keyboard settings for finer tweaking.
macOS: New Recovery Lock Password settings to set and rotate firmware passwords, and File Provider controls for external volume and remote syncing, handy for keeping Macs locked down.
Windows: A policy to remove Microsoft Copilot app is now available, and Edge gains standardized zoom behavior and a preview enrollment type, though several Edge policies are now marked deprecated.
2026-03-26.watchOut: 133 description rewrites and 31 renames are mostly cleanups, but the deprecation warnings on several Edge policies signal they might stop working later; also, Remote Remediation applicability changed and macOS Tamper protection now includes microsoftSense, so review Defender configurations.

2026-03-03.headline: Quiet day: no settings added or removed, just category housekeeping; three new buckets appeared, ten got touched. If you blinked, you missed it.
highlights: Three new Settings Catalog categories: 'Custom', 'When sending a message', and 'Microsoft One Note 2016'
Ten existing categories were tweaked, including Printing, OneNote Options, and several Chrome-related ones
No settings themselves changed, so existing policies should be untouched
2026-03-03.watchOut: Nothing to worry about; category changes might affect how you search or filter, but no behavior impact on deployed settings.

2026-03-02.headline: Quiet day: no settings added or removed, just some category housekeeping and three new category names that might mean something eventually.
highlights: No new or removed settings across any platform; purely metadata changes today.
Three new categories appeared: 'Custom', 'When sending a message', and 'Microsoft One Note 2016' – likely placeholder shells for future settings.
Ten existing categories got tweaked (renamed or reorganized), including Printing, OneNote Options, and Safe Browsing settings; nothing functionally changed.
2026-03-02.watchOut: No admins affected; this is just Microsoft tidying up the catalog structure.

2026-03-01.headline: Windows gets a pile of new settings: Office macro lockdowns, Edge HTTPS-only enforcement, and passkey storage, a security admin's early Christmas.
highlights: Windows: 10 new macro security settings (block COM/VSTO add-ins, restrict trusted documents, require signed macros); worth enforcing before someone enables a malicious macro.
Windows: Edge can now force HTTPS-Only Mode on users or devices; consider setting it to 'enabled' to avoid plaintext traffic.
Windows: Passkeys can now be saved to the password manager; a move toward passwordless, but check your policy before letting users do it.
Windows: Idle detection site controls for Edge (allow/block lists) give you more visibility into background browser activity.
2026-03-01.watchOut: No removals or setting changes, so nothing breaks; the 10 categories with metadata updates look like cosmetic renames. All additions are Windows-only, other platforms are untouched.

2026-03.headline: March adds Local Network Access controls to keep websites off your intranet, plus a wave of Apple Intelligence toggles worth a look.
2026-03.overview: Four update days and roughly 140 new settings, most of them noise. The real story is the new browser-level Local Network Access controls on Windows and a fresh set of Apple Intelligence and cryptography settings. Also, a bunch of Edge settings got officially deprecated, so if you rely on them, now is the time to plan.

sections.body: The big add is the Network settings category with 22 settings to control Local Network Access (LNA) from the browser. You can now block or allow sites to request local network endpoints and the local device, plus override IP address space mappings and handle LNA in subframes. That's a solid security win against drive-by scans of your internal network. Also new: cryptography compliance policies to prefer specific TLS ciphers and key exchange algorithms, plus a heap of Outlook and OneNote settings under 'When sending a message' and 'Custom'. And watch out: many Edge policies got the (Deprecated) tag in this month's display name refresh, so check if any of your assignments depend on them.

Apple got a new Intelligence Settings category (that's the Apple Intelligence controls) with options to force on-device dictation, allow or disallow Smart Replies, Image Playground, Genmoji, and more. Also new Keyboard and Siri settings, plus File Provider and Recovery Lock Password for macOS. The applicability changes are interesting: several enrollment settings (Intune authentication method, User affinity, Await final configuration) now also apply to macOS, not just iOS, and some macOS Defender settings now support microsoftSense, so they can be managed via Defender for Endpoint. Existing profiles might suddenly apply to more devices, so review your assignment filters.

2026-03.watchOut: Mass deprecation of Edge settings (dozens got the deprecated label) and some macOS applicability expansions could change which devices receive policies. Also, if you're using the old 'Compose' Edge policy, it's been renamed and the description changed, so re-verify your config.

2026-02-25.headline: Apple renames Rapid Security Responses to Background Security Improvements, macOS gets offline antivirus mirrors, and a few settings finally get 'Deprecated' slapped on them.
highlights: macOS: New Antivirus engine settings let you set a mirror URL and enable offline security intelligence updates, handy for Macs on lockdown networks.
iOS/macOS: Software Update Settings now talk about Background Security Improvements instead of Rapid Security Responses; same toggles, new vocabulary.
Deprecation party: Force Delayed Software Updates, Software Update Settings (iOS), and AirPlay Device ID all get the axe, so check your profiles.
2026-02-25.watchOut: If you're using the deprecated settings, start planning migration. Also, the RSR to Background Security Improvements shift might change what users see; verify your update policies still behave.

2026-02.headline: macOS sneaks in offline antivirus update controls, while everything else is just housekeeping and deprecation flags.
2026-02.overview: One update day this month, and it was mostly quiet. The only real capability gain is macOS support for hosting security intelligence updates on an internal mirror, which is a gift for air-gapped fleets. Everything else is description rewrites, label cleanups, and some deprecation warnings, so don't clear your calendar.

sections.body: Windows got no new toys this month. The Remote Remediation settings (still Windows Insiders only) had their descriptions rewritten to clarify dependency and ordering, and the embarrassing '[Pending fix]' labels were finally scrubbed. The one thing actually worth your attention: 'Enable Windows Restore' lost its 'Windows Insiders only' tag, which might mean it's about to go mainstream. If you've been holding off on deploying that, maybe start planning.

The headline here is macOS gaining two Antivirus engine settings that let you point devices at a local mirror for security intelligence updates, with optional signature verification. That's a nice win for environments that can't reach the internet on demand. Elsewhere, iOS and macOS both saw AirPlay gain a 'Device Name' setting while 'Device ID' got the deprecated hat, and the Software Update Settings descriptions swapped 'Rapid Security Responses' for 'Background Security Improvements', which reads like a brand refresh more than a functional change. Also, 'Force Delayed Software Updates' is now officially marked deprecated, so it's time to check if you're leaning on it.

2026-02.watchOut: The deprecation flags: 'Force Delayed Software Updates' and AirPlay 'Device ID' are both marked deprecated, so audit any policies that reference them. The Rapid Security Responses to Background Security Improvements wording is just a description update, but it might hint at a future rebrand, so keep your ears open.
